about: Battle of Wits (was Quiz Battle; Henry, Nov 19) built-in question sets per level (written for Kru). 5 sets of 10 per level; shuffled every game; "All topics" mixes all 50. choices + answer index = multiple choice; answer text = short answer. why = the short explanation shown when the class checks the answers. hidden = the hidden bonuses (2 per round, revealed before the tally; needs = only for rounds with short / choice questions; {n} = a question number, {letter} = a first letter of a right answer). Rounds of 5, played by the shared Battle engine.

questions.why: "Yesterday" means the past. The past of "go" is "went".

questions.q: She ___ a sandwich for lunch yesterday.
questions.why: The past of "eat" is "ate" (an irregular verb).
"Buy" is irregular: buy → bought. ("Brought" is the past of "bring".)
After "didn't" we use the base verb: didn't watch.

questions.q: ___ you see the movie last weekend?
questions.why: Questions in the past simple start with "Did".
"Swim" is irregular: swim → swam.
"Yesterday" = past. Regular verbs add -ed: play → played.
"Mom" is one person (she), so the past of "be" is "was".

questions.q: The children ___ tired after the trip.
questions.why: "The children" are many people (they), so we use "were".
Negative past simple: didn't + base verb. "Ate" becomes "didn't eat".
A mango is a fruit. A carrot is a vegetable.
You sleep in a bedroom.

questions.q: What do you wear on your feet?
questions.why: Shoes go on your feet. A hat goes on your head.
A cow says "moo".
Doctors work in hospitals.

questions.q: What color is the sky on a sunny day?
questions.why: On a sunny day the sky is blue.
The opposite of "big" is "small".

questions.q: How many days are there in a week?
questions.why: Monday to Sunday: 7 days in a week.
A verb is an action word. "Run" is an action.
12 is spelled t-w-e-l-v-e.
"She" + present simple: add -s. walk → walks.
"I" uses "don't" for negatives: I don't like…
"Your brother" = he, so the question starts with "Does".
"My cat" = it: add -s. eat → eats.
"We" uses the base verb: we study.

questions.q: Write it for "he": I watch TV.
questions.why: He/she/it: add -es after -ch. watch → watches.
With he/she/it, "have" becomes "has".
"She" needs -es: go → goes.
"They" uses the base verb: they live.
He + doesn't + base verb: "likes" becomes "doesn't like".
A carrot is a vegetable. The others are fruits.
Birds have wings, so they can fly.
Fish live in water.
Milk comes from cows.
Juice is something you drink.

questions.q: What animal is very big and gray with a long nose?
questions.why: Elephants are big and gray with a long nose (a trunk).
Chocolate is sweet. Lemons are sour and chili is hot.
A baby dog is a puppy. A baby cat is a kitten.
A duck says "quack".

questions.q: What is the yellow fruit that monkeys love?
questions.why: Monkeys love bananas, and they are yellow.
Inside a box = in the box.
We use "in" with months: in May.
We use "at" with clock times: at 8 o'clock.
"What" asks about a thing, like your name.
"Where" asks about a place.

questions.q: Write the question word: "___ old are you?"
questions.why: "How old" asks about age.

questions.q: The book is ___ the table. (on top)
questions.why: On top of something = on.
"Who" asks about a person.
We use "on" with days: on Saturday.

questions.q: Write the question word: "___ is your birthday?" (a date)
questions.why: "When" asks about a time or a date.

questions.q: At 8 p.m. last night I ___ TV.
questions.why: An action in progress at a time in the past: was/were + -ing.
"They" uses "were": were sleeping.

questions.q: While she ___ home, it started to rain.
questions.why: "She" uses "was": was walking (in progress when the rain started).

questions.q: What ___ you doing at 9 o'clock last night?
questions.why: "You" uses "were": What were you doing?

questions.q: We were playing soccer ___ the teacher arrived.
questions.why: A long action, then a short one: "when" + the short action.
Negative past continuous: wasn't + -ing.
"I" uses "was" + -ing: I was eating.

questions.q: ___ I was cooking, my brother was cleaning.
questions.why: "While" joins two long actions happening at the same time.

questions.q: It was raining, ___ we stayed at home.
questions.why: "So" gives the result: it was raining, so we stayed home.

questions.q: Write the past continuous: they / swim
questions.why: "They" + were + verb-ing: they were swimming.

questions.q: Which one is a document with your photo, for traveling to other countries?
questions.why: A passport has your photo and lets you travel to other countries.

questions.q: You put your clothes in a ___ for a trip.
questions.why: A suitcase holds your clothes for a trip.

questions.q: Something you buy to remember a trip is a ___.
questions.why: A souvenir is something you buy to remember a place.
Planes take off and land at an airport.

questions.q: You use ___ to protect your skin from the sun.
questions.why: Sunscreen protects your skin from the sun.

questions.answer: Any island: Phuket, Koh Samui, Koh Chang, Koh Lanta…
questions.why: Phuket, Koh Samui, Koh Chang and Koh Lanta are all Thai islands.

questions.q: A person who visits a place on vacation is a ___.
questions.why: A tourist visits a place on vacation.

choices: I goed to Krabi last year.
I go to Krabi last year.
I went to Krabi last year.
I going to Krabi last year.
questions.why: "Last year" = past. The past of "go" is "went".

questions.q: You sleep in a ___ when you go camping.
questions.why: When you go camping, you sleep in a tent.
"Fly" is irregular: fly → flew.

questions.q: An elephant is ___ than a dog.
questions.why: Comparing two things: big → bigger (double the g) + than.

questions.q: This is the ___ day of the year!
questions.why: "The ___ of the year" = superlative: hot → hottest.
Words ending in -y: change y to i and add -er: busier.

questions.q: English is ___ than math for me.
questions.why: easy → easier (y becomes i, add -er).

questions.q: That was the ___ movie I have ever seen.
questions.why: "Bad" is irregular: bad, worse, worst.
"Good" is irregular: good, better, best.

choices: She is more tall than me.
questions.why: Short adjectives add -er: tall → taller than.

questions.q: My little sister is ___ than me. (young)
questions.why: young → younger (comparing two people).

questions.q: This hotel is the ___ in town.
questions.why: Long adjectives use "the most": the most expensive.
Long adjectives: the most + adjective. the most beautiful.

questions.q: I was tired, ___ I went to bed early.
questions.why: "So" shows the result: tired, so I went to bed.

questions.q: I stayed at home ___ it was raining.
questions.why: "Because" gives the reason: it was raining.

questions.q: ___ it was cold, we went swimming.
questions.why: "Although" shows a surprise: cold, but we still swam.

questions.q: I like tea, ___ I don't like coffee.
questions.why: "But" joins two different ideas: like tea / don't like coffee.

questions.q: First we had lunch, ___ we went to the beach.
questions.why: "Then" shows what happened next.

questions.answer: Any good ending, e.g. because I passed the test.
questions.why: "Because" gives a reason. Any reason that makes sense is right.
"Or" gives a choice: tea or coffee?

questions.q: ___ I was sleeping, someone knocked on the door.
questions.why: "While" = during a long action.

questions.q: She studied hard, ___ she passed the exam.
questions.why: "So" shows the result: studied hard, so she passed.

questions.q: Join with "but": "The hotel was nice. The food was bad."
questions.answer: The hotel was nice, but the food was bad.
questions.why: Put a comma before "but": …nice, but the food was bad.

questions.q: You catch a train at a ___.
questions.why: Trains stop at a station.
A library lends books.
A boat travels on water.

questions.q: You can see old things from history in a ___.
questions.why: Museums show old things from history.

questions.q: We went to Chiang Mai ___ train.
questions.why: We say "by" + transport: by train, by bus.

questions.q: Where do you go when you are very ill?
questions.why: When you are very ill, you go to a hospital.
A pharmacy sells medicine.
A tuk-tuk has three wheels.
Banks change money.

questions.q: Name a place where you can watch a movie.
questions.why: You watch movies at a movie theater.

questions.q: If it rains tomorrow, we ___ at home.
questions.why: First conditional: if + present, will + verb.

questions.q: If I ___ rich, I would buy a big house.
questions.why: Second conditional (not real): if + were, would + verb.

questions.q: If you heat water to 100°C, it ___.
questions.why: Zero conditional (always true): if + present, present.

questions.q: If she had studied, she ___ the exam.
questions.why: Third conditional (past): if + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

questions.q: What would you do if you ___ a million baht?
questions.why: Second conditional: if + past simple (won), would + verb.

questions.q: Finish: "If I were you, I ___ (go) to the doctor."
questions.why: Advice: "If I were you, I would…"

choices: If I see him, I will tell him.
If I will see him, I tell him.
If I saw him, I will tell him.
If I see him, I would told him.
questions.why: First conditional: if + present (see), will + verb (will tell).

questions.q: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.
questions.why: "Unless" = if not. Result: will miss.

questions.q: I wouldn't do that if I ___ you.
questions.why: Second conditional with "I": if I were you.

questions.q: Finish: "If I had more time, I ___ (learn) Korean."
questions.why: Second conditional: if + past (had), would + verb (would learn).

questions.q: "It's a piece of cake" means it is ___.
questions.why: "A piece of cake" = very easy.

questions.q: "I'm feeling under the weather" means I feel ___.
questions.why: "Under the weather" = a little ill.
We "make" a mistake (not "do").
We "do" someone a favor.
"Once in a blue moon" = very rarely.

questions.q: Finish the idiom: "Break the ___" (start a friendly conversation).
questions.why: "Break the ice" = start a friendly conversation.
We say "heavy rain", not "strong rain".
"Hit the books" = study hard.
We "make" a decision.
"Actions speak louder than words" = what you do matters more than what you say.

questions.q: The man ___ lives next door is a doctor.
questions.why: "Who" is for people.

questions.q: This is the house ___ I was born.
questions.why: "Where" is for places.

questions.q: The phone ___ I bought is broken.
questions.why: "That" can be used for things.

questions.q: She's the girl ___ brother is famous.
questions.why: "Whose" shows something belongs to someone: her brother.

questions.q: The movie ___ we watched was boring.
questions.why: "Which" is for things, like a movie.

questions.q: Join with "who": "I have a friend. She speaks French."
questions.answer: I have a friend who speaks French.
questions.why: "Who" replaces "she": I have a friend who speaks French.

choices: The book which I read was great.
The book who I read was great.
The book where I read was great.
The book whose I read was great.
questions.why: "Which" is for things. "Who" is only for people.

questions.q: Bangkok, ___ is the capital of Thailand, is very busy.
questions.why: After a comma (extra information) we use "which", not "that".

questions.q: Do you know anyone ___ can fix computers?
questions.why: "Who" is for people: anyone who can fix…

questions.q: Join with "where": "This is the café. We met there."
questions.answer: This is the café where we met.
questions.why: "Where" replaces "there": the café where we met.
"Give up" = stop trying.

questions.q: Please ___ the lights when you leave. (switch off)
questions.why: "Turn off" = switch off.

questions.q: Can you ___ my cat while I'm away?
questions.why: "Look after" = take care of.

questions.q: I need to ___ this word in the dictionary.
questions.why: "Look up" = find a word in a dictionary.

questions.q: We've ___ milk. Can you buy some?
questions.why: "Run out of" = have none left.
"Find out" = discover information.
A plane "takes off" when it leaves the ground.

questions.q: She ___ her mother: they look the same.
questions.why: "Take after" = look or act like a parent.

questions.q: Our car ___ on the way to Hua Hin.
questions.why: "Break down" = stop working (a car or machine).
"Carry on" = continue.
happy → happiness: the y changes to i, then add -ness.
danger + -ous = dangerous.
"Possible" takes "im-": impossible.
decide → decision (the noun ends in -sion).
"Honest" takes "dis-": dishonest.
beauty → beautiful: y changes to i, then add -ful.
careful + -ly = carefully (keep both l's).

questions.q: A person who teaches is a ___.
questions.why: teach + -er = teacher (a person who does the job).
free + -dom = freedom.
"Legal" takes "il-": illegal.

intro.title: Battle of Wits
text: 5 questions per round. Your team writes each answer on ONE board.
No shouting answers: keep them secret!

intro.title: Be quick!
text: When it ends, the next question comes by itself.

intro.title: Check together
text: After 5 questions, we check every answer together.
Mark each answer on your board: ✓ or ✗.

intro.title: Hidden bonuses!
text: Before you count, 2 secret bonuses are revealed.
A long word? A full sentence? Extra points!

intro.title: Count your points
text: 1 point for each right answer, plus your bonuses.
Tell your teacher your team’s total.

hidden.name: Golden Question
hidden.text: Question {n} was secretly worth double! Right? +1 more.

hidden.name: Comeback
hidden.text: The team in last place gets +2!

hidden.name: Neatest Board
hidden.text: Your teacher picks the neatest board: +2!

hidden.name: Spelling Star
hidden.text: Every word on your board spelled right? +2!

hidden.name: Long Word
hidden.text: An answer with a word of 10+ letters? +1!

hidden.name: Syllable Hunter
hidden.text: An answer with a word of 3+ syllables? +1!

hidden.name: Full Sentence
hidden.text: One answer written as a full sentence? +1!

hidden.name: Lucky Letter
hidden.text: +1 for each right answer that starts with the letter {letter}!

hidden.name: Letter B Luck
hidden.text: +1 for each right answer that was B!

M.1.quote: yesterday i go to the market and buyed two apple.
M.1.answer: Yesterday I went to the market and bought two apples.

M.1.q: Rewrite as ONE sentence starting with 'Although'.
M.1.quote: It was raining. We went to the park. We had a great time.
M.1.answer: Although it was raining, we went to the park and had a great time.
M.1.why: 'Although' + clause, comma, then the main clause. Accept small differences if the grammar and the comma are right.

M.1.q: Write the correct form of EVERY verb in brackets.
M.1.quote: If I ___ (be) rich, I ___ (buy) a house, but I ___ (be) not rich.
M.1.hint: Write the three words, in order
M.1.why: Second conditional: if + past (were), would + base verb. The last gap is a real present fact: am.

M.1.q: Change the whole sentence to the PAST.
M.1.quote: Every day she gets up at six, makes breakfast and walks to school.
M.1.answer: Every day she got up at six, made breakfast and walked to school.
M.1.why: got up, made and walked: two irregular verbs and one regular verb.

M.1.q: Put the words in order to make TWO correct sentences.
M.1.quote: park / went / to / the / we / Sunday / on   •   playing / were / children / the / happily
M.1.hint: Write both sentences with capitals and periods
M.1.answer: We went to the park on Sunday. The children were playing happily.
M.1.why: Sentence 1: subject + verb + place + time. Sentence 2: past continuous (were playing).

M.1.q: Complete EVERY gap with ONE word.
M.1.quote: She ___ lived here ___ 2015, so she has known her neighbors ___ ten years.
M.1.hint: Write the three words, in order
M.1.why: Present perfect: has lived; since + a point in time (2015); for + a length of time (ten years).

M.2.quote: Last weekend my family and I has visited a beautifull temple. It were very old, and there was many tourist. I enjoyed it so much that i want to go again.
M.2.answer: Last weekend my family and I visited a beautiful temple. It was very old, and there were many tourists. I enjoyed it so much that I want to go again.
M.2.why: visited (not has visited), beautiful, It was, there were, tourists, I (capital).

M.2.q: Join the three sentences into ONE sentence with a relative clause.
M.2.quote: My neighbor is a doctor. She works at the city hospital. She is very kind.
M.2.answer: My neighbor, who is a doctor and works at the city hospital, is very kind.
M.2.why: A relative clause (who ...) with commas for extra information. Accept other correct versions.

M.2.quote: They have cancelled the match because the rain flooded the field.
M.2.answer: The match has been cancelled because the field was flooded by the rain.
M.2.why: Present perfect passive (has been cancelled) and past passive (was flooded).

M.2.q: Put EVERY verb in brackets in the correct tense.
M.2.quote: By the time we ___ (arrive), the film ___ (already start).
M.2.why: Past simple for the later action; past perfect for the earlier one.

M.2.q: Add ALL the capital letters and punctuation.
M.2.quote: although it was late tom decided to finish his homework he opened his book took a deep breath and started writing
M.2.answer: Although it was late, Tom decided to finish his homework. He opened his book, took a deep breath, and started writing.
M.2.why: A comma after the 'although' clause, a period, and commas in the list of three actions.

M.2.quote: "I'll call you tomorrow if I'm not working," she said to me.
M.2.answer: She told me that she would call me the next day if she wasn't working.
M.2.why: will becomes would, tomorrow becomes the next day, am not becomes was not.

M.3.q: Rewrite the sentence with 'Had' at the start.
M.3.quote: If I had known the truth, I would have acted differently.
M.3.answer: Had I known the truth, I would have acted differently.
M.3.why: 'Had I known' = 'If I had known' (third conditional, no 'if').

M.3.quote: Despite of the rain, we have went to the beach, and the sea were warmer than I have expected.
M.3.answer: Despite the rain, we went to the beach, and the sea was warmer than I had expected.
M.3.why: Despite (no 'of'), went (not have went), was (not were), had expected (past perfect).

M.3.q: Join into ONE sentence using a PARTICIPLE clause.
M.3.quote: She opened the door. She saw a strange package on the floor.
M.3.answer: Opening the door, she saw a strange package on the floor.
M.3.why: A participle clause (Opening ...) shares the subject of the main clause.

M.3.q: Rewrite in the PASSIVE with a reporting verb.
M.3.quote: People say that the company is losing millions.
M.3.answer: The company is said to be losing millions. (or: It is said that the company is losing millions.)
M.3.why: Passive reporting structure: is said to + infinitive, or It is said that...

M.3.q: Fill ALL four gaps with the correct form of the word in brackets.
M.3.quote: The ___ (decide) was a ___ (surprise) to everyone, but the ___ (organize) explained it ___ (clear).
M.3.hint: Write the four words, in order
M.3.why: A noun after 'The', a noun after 'a', a plural noun as the subject, an adverb after the verb.

M.3.quote: I'm sorry I didn't call her yesterday. It's too late now.
M.3.answer: I wish I had called her yesterday.
M.3.why: A regret about the past: wish + past perfect.
